description:
The least-TTFT joint COMPARATOR arm (config.md 9.3), as TWO plugin registrations that reuse the focal arm's Handler, Picker, Policy, and decider wholesale and supply ONE thing: the per-candidate cost function. least-ttft-joint-handler carries ProfileHandler (Pick + ProcessResults) plus PreRequest and ResponseBodyProcessor and owns the shared state; least-ttft-joint-picker carries Filter + Picker and runs the argmin over D local plus D*P disaggregated candidates. The split is forced by the target's interfaces, not chosen: ProfileHandler.Pick and Picker.Pick share a method name with different signatures (pkg/epp/framework/interface/scheduling/plugins.go:47, :77). Filter is required rather than incidental, because Picker.Pick receives only []*ScoredEndpoint and no request. Objective: argmin over (decode endpoint d, prefill placement p) of the arriving request's own projected TTFT -- local = tAdmD + nChunks*tIterD + Wp + postProcessing, disaggregated = max(tAdmP + nChunksP*tIterP + wpP + c_xfer, tAdmD) + tIterFirstDecode + postProcessing. It carries no backlog drift, no SLO virtual queues, no externality over residents, and NO tau at all.

HOW THE VERBATIM-COPY CONTRACT IS SATISFIED, and this is the central design decision of this arm. config.md 9.3 and algorithms/least_ttft_joint.go:47-96 require roughly forty symbols -- Coeffs and every method, the admission contexts and every estimator, the whole scheduler rollout, the projection helpers, the shadow-table reads, the types, the adapters -- to be VERBATIM COPIES of the focal arm's, on the stated ground that 'a re-derived-but-slightly-different estimator would silently destroy the attribution argument while every test still passed'. This port satisfies it by SHARING rather than by copying, which is strictly stronger: a copy can drift under an edit to one side, and drift is exactly the failure named. Every listed symbol has exactly ONE implementation and both arms reach it through causalsloexternality.Eval, a set of one-line delegations to Policy. There is one Coeffs, one rollforward estimator, one shadow table, one candidate enumeration, one argmin. THE leastttftjoint PACKAGE CONTAINS NO PHYSICS: objective.go computes only the composition of Eval-supplied operands, and plugin.go is 88 lines of type constants and factory wiring. The seam mirrors the simulation's own shape, where decideJoint's costFn is swapped per rule (sim/edpp.go:1334, with the least-ttft assignment at :1453).

THE SHARED SEAM, which is the modification a reviewer should scrutinise. Two files were ADDED to the causalsloexternality package -- arm.go (Objective, Arm, Eval, and the arm-parameterised factory constructors) and evalfixture.go (EvalFixture, an exported test seam) -- and five existing files were changed additively: policy.go (Policy gains an objective field; decide calls objective.Cost instead of scoreCandidate, and takes enumeration order and capacity liveness from the objective), handler.go (Handler gains an arm field; HandlerFactory becomes NewHandlerFactory(FocalArm)), picker.go (same for PickerFactory and PickerConfigParser, plus the cross-arm binding guard), config.go (validate takes an Objective and gates the SLO-value half in both directions), and README.md (a new 'Serving both experimental arms' section, plus one corrected paragraph -- see below). Three focal test files were updated mechanically for the new validate and newPolicy signatures: config_test.go, overlay_test.go, policy_test.go. THE FOCAL ARM'S BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED: its objective is now focalObjective{}, whose Cost is scoreCandidate(...).total, it declares ScorerFirstEnumeration true and ReadsSLOValueConfig true, and its whole test suite passes unmodified apart from those signature updates.

Because the whole causalsloexternality directory is still untracked, git sees those edits as part of the created tree rather than as a diff, which is why files_created lists both packages and files_modified lists only runner.go. The focal-package changes are therefore stated here rather than inferable from a diff.

FILES_CREATED IS THE UNION ACROSS BOTH ARMS, 35 paths, AND SO IS THE FOCAL ARM'S, DELIBERATELY. The two arms share one Go package and one registration file, so neither arm's source subset compiles alone and the treatment source set is the union rather than a per-arm slice. restore_baseline deletes exactly one arm's files_created and git-checkouts its files_modified (pipeline/lib/source_toggle.py:17-43), so a per-arm subset leaves the other arm's files behind as orphans referencing deleted symbols. MEASURED, not reasoned: with the focal manifest declaring only its own 29 files, simulating restore_baseline(causalsloexternality) left this arm's 6 files on disk and the gate's own `go vet ./pkg/.../profilehandler/... ./cmd/epp/runner/...` failed with 'no required module provides package .../causalsloexternality'. With the union declared on both manifests, simulating restore_baseline in EITHER direction leaves 0 files under both package directories and both `go vet` and `go build ./cmd/epp/...` pass, and restoring the treatment from either arm's generated tree reproduces the checkout byte for byte. The two generated trees are byte-identical over all 36 declared paths, so materialising them in either order is idempotent -- which was the second consequence the round-1 review named.

WHAT THE COMPARATOR DIVERGES IN, exhaustively, so any other divergence is a defect:
  1. THE OBJECTIVE. As above.
  2. ENUMERATION ORDER. Plain ascending-ID, not scorer-first. Upstream's least-ttft branch iterates decodeSnaps directly (sim/edpp.go:1456) while scorerFirstSnapshots is applied only in the SLO-externality and causal-VaR branches, its own doc calling it 'the causal-VaR equality tie-break order' (sim/edpp.go:2176-2178). It is a tie-break order, so copying the focal arm's would change which candidate wins an EXACT tie -- silently, and only sometimes, and exact ties are the norm during warmup. Asserted by TestScorerPreferenceReordersTheFocalArmButNotThisOne, which runs BOTH arms through the shared decider with a preference injected and pins each one's first candidate.
  3. THE CONFIG SURFACE. A strict subset: no v, ablation, activeWorkload, workloadTargets, or capacity. This is ENFORCED, not documented. Those keys are KNOWN to the shared Config struct, so DisallowUnknownFields accepts them and only an arm-aware check can refuse them; Config.rejectSLOValueConfig makes any of them a startup error. The trap it closes is concrete: an operator copies the focal overlay to make this one and tunes tau in it, would be tuning nothing, and the arm-vs-arm comparison would be read as if they had. Consequently there is NO decomposed switch on this arm -- config.md 10's knob is DecomposedSLOExternality, a focal-arm switch, and the +0.0485 decode-first check belongs to the focal arm, whose enumeration is scorer-first. Everything else in the parameter block is byte-identical to the focal arm's, asserted against the shipped file by TestOverlayIsCommonModeWithTheFocalArmOutsideTheObjective over coefficients, transfer model, engine agreement, shadow table, signal bindings, admission estimator, and post-processing.

NEW SILENT-FAILURE MODE FOUND AND CLOSED: THE CROSS-ARM BINDING. Both arms are the same Go type, so raw.(*Handler) succeeds for either and the picker's existing type assertion no longer distinguishes them. A least-ttft-joint-picker bound to a causal-slo-externality-handler would construct successfully and then run the FOCAL objective -- the objective lives in the Policy the handler owns -- while every log line, every plugin_type metric label, and the treatment overlay's own name reported the comparator. The reported arm-vs-arm comparison would be a comparison of one arm with itself. newPicker now compares handler.arm.HandlerType against the picker's arm and refuses, with the mismatch named; TestPickerRejectsTheOtherArmsHandler and TestOverlayPickerNamesThisArmsHandler cover it.

WHY A PICKER AND NOT A SCORER, for this arm's own reason as well as the inherited one. A Scorer returns a per-endpoint map with no way to name a PAIR; and every scorer contribution passes through enforceScoreRange, which clamps to [0,1] (pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler_profile.go:212, :364). This objective is a LATENCY IN MICROSECONDS -- non-negative and unbounded above -- so clamping would collapse essentially every candidate to one score, destroying the ranking rather than degrading it. The focal arm faces the same hazard because its J is signed and unbounded. runPickerPlugin never clamps. TestCostIsAnUnboundedMicrosecondLatency pins the magnitude so the hazard stays concrete.

METRICS ARE SHARED DELIBERATELY. The collectors keep their causal_slo_externality_* names and are distinguished by plugin_name and plugin_type labels, which is what the focal arm's metrics.go was already built for ('so the two arms can be told apart in the same EPP', and registerMetrics is idempotent for exactly this reason). It makes the D1 and D8 rate comparison config.md requires a single label query rather than a join across two metric families. The name prefix is a cosmetic inheritance and is called out in the package README rather than papered over.

DECLARED DEGRADATIONS. D2, D4, D5, D6, D7, D8, and D9 are inherited unchanged through the shared machinery, and D2c is NOT inherited (no kernel here reads ArrivalUs, FirstTokenUs, or TTFTSet). Two need arm-specific statements:

D1 -- the scheduler rollout is unobtainable and rollforward substitutes, with the same required counter. ITS DIRECTION IS NOT A SINGLE SIGN FOR THIS OBJECTIVE, and the focal arm's one-line summary is deliberately NOT copied over. Local adds tAdmD with slope 1 while disaggregated takes max(remoteLead, tAdmD), so when tAdmD dominates the max, understating it is charged identically to both placements and CANCELS; when remoteLead dominates, the disaggregated candidate is insensitive to tAdmD, so understating it lowers ONLY the local candidate -- biasing toward LOCAL, opposite to the focal arm. The toward-remote direction survives only through the tAdmP channel and only while remoteLead dominates. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ATTRIBUTION ARGUMENT: 'both arms inherit D1 identically so the comparison stays fair' is NOT a claim this port makes. Under decode-side congestion -- the regime the high-load and burst cohorts target -- D1 shifts the two arms' local/remote splits by different amounts, so the comparison is fair only where the substitution counter shows the same estimator regime on both arms. Also worth recording: the rollout was the LIVE path upstream for this rule rather than a fallback, so on the target both arms run an estimator that produced none of the numbers in sim_results/.

D5 -- c_xfer is unmeasured, and it matters MORE here than in the focal arm, because there is no externality term to partially offset a mis-priced transfer, so it moves this arm's decisions systematically. TestTransferPriceEntersOnlyTheDisaggregatedCandidate pins its single entry point. It is not the only size-dependent remote price: the re-timed B+1 first decode iteration also scales with input length, so prompt size prices the remote path through two channels.

CORE MODIFICATION: cmd/epp/runner/runner.go, 34 insertions for this arm's code (one import plus two registration calls) within 75 total insertions and 0 deletions in the file across both arms, the balance being the shared explanatory comment, purely additive -- one import plus two registration calls with an explanatory comment. No existing line is changed. No extension point can replace it: plugin types reach the config loader only through the process-global fwkplugin.Registry, which this in-tree binary populates in Runner.registerInTreePlugins, and the treatment overlay switches the arm on by NAMING those types, so without the registration the types are unresolvable and the EPP refuses to start. The picker uses RegisterWithPluginDependencies with this arm's PickerConfigParser, because instantiatePlugins constructs in TOPOLOGICAL order over the plugin DAG (pkg/epp/config/loader/configloader.go:244-250) rather than in config order; with plain Register both plugins sit at in-degree 0 and their order comes from ranging a Go map (pkg/epp/util/utils.go:42-46), which is a nondeterministic crashloop. TestShippedTreatmentConfigLoadsWithPickerDeclaredFirst drives the real loader twelve times with the picker declared first.

Registered StabilityBeta. THE FOCAL BLOCK'S FALSE CLAIM WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE, comment-only, at the team lead's direction, and the corrected paragraph now covers BOTH arms so there is one accurate statement rather than two competing ones. The claim that --allow-experimental-plugins 'is not expressible through the scenario overlay this arm is deployed from' is wrong: router.epp.flags is read into $eppFlags at config/charts/routerlib/templates/_deployment.yaml:8 and rendered as --<key>=<value> args on the `- name: epp` container (:74) by the range at :116-120, documented at config/charts/routerlib/values.yaml:29-32, and llm-d-benchmark's router-values template passes the scenario's whole router block through. So Alpha is not ruled out by the deployment path. It is ruled out by what it would cost: an Alpha registration makes every arm's overlay carry a required router.epp.flags.allow-experimental-plugins field whose omission prevents the EPP from starting, and the failure lands only after the image is built and pushed, because nothing in the build or test gate instantiates plugins. Nothing but that startup gate reads the stability level, so Beta costs nothing in behaviour. The four registration calls are byte-identical to the focal arm's approved snapshot: stripping comments and blank lines, the only code difference between this runner.go and snapshots/causalsloexternality/v4/cmd/epp/runner/runner.go is one import and this arm's two Register calls.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE FOCAL ARM'S README, declared because it is an edit to already-approved work. Its 'Why two plugins' section stated that the handler must be declared first because 'plugins are instantiated in configuration order ... so by-name references resolve backward only'. That is contradicted by the loader, by the package's own code comments, and by dependency_test.go: order comes from a topological sort over the plugin DAG and position in the list does not matter. Since my arm depends on exactly that mechanism and the paragraph would lead an operator to reorder a list that does not need reordering, I replaced it with the accurate statement. One paragraph, no behaviour change.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS PORT. Upstream rewriting registerInTreePlugins or moving registration out of cmd/epp/runner/runner.go; a change to Register/RegisterWithPluginDependencies, to the pluginRef tag convention read by findPluginDependencies, or to TopologicalSort's edge direction; a change to enforceScoreRange or to whether runPickerPlugin clamps, which would break the Picker-not-Scorer argument for both arms; a change to ProfileRunResult.TargetEndpoints away from a slice, which would break carrying both picks from one picker run. And specific to the shared seam: any future edit to Eval must be made in the shared package rather than re-derived in an arm, because an arm that computes its own physics converts a controlled comparison into two unrelated algorithms and no test in either arm would fail.

NO PACKAGE README for leastttftjoint, deliberately. objective.go's package comment is the canonical location for what is arm-specific, the focal package's README now covers the shared machinery and both arms' types, and config.md and the bundle README carry the experiment-level facts. A third copy would be the duplication this codebase's style rules forbid, and the risk is that the copies drift on exactly the degradation directions that differ between the arms.

VALIDATION RUN, all nine gate commands green: make build (podman builder, epp and sidecar); go vet (0); golangci-lint --config=./.golangci.yml over both trees (0 issues); go test -count=1 on causalsloexternality and on leastttftjoint; go test -count=1 -race over all of profilehandler/ (six packages); go test ./pkg/epp/scheduling/...; go test ./pkg/epp/framework/...; go build ./cmd/epp/.... The generated overlay is checked by tests that read the shipped YAML from outside the Go module, which is why -count=1 is required rather than stylistic: those tests also pass against the PRIOR v0.9.0 translation's leastttftjoint overlay, whose handler parameter block is content-identical to this one -- an independent confirmation of the config subset.

RAISED BY THE EXPERT AND WEIGHED, NOT DEFERRED. The expert's answer argued that sharing causalsloexternality.Config is forbidden by the specification, on two grounds: that it puts v, ablation, activeWorkload, workloadTargets, and capacity into this arm's overlay surface as fields with no consumer -- the reader trap the spec names -- and that Config.validate REQUIRES activeWorkload and positive tauTtftUs/tauE2eUs, so the comparator's overlay would have to state thresholds it never reads or fail to start. Its recommendation was a separate Config and validate for this arm.

The second ground is answered by the seam: validate is now arm-aware and REJECTS those five keys for this arm rather than requiring them, so the comparator's overlay states no threshold and cannot. The expert's reading was of the unmodified focal package. The first ground is answered at the level that matters: the trap the spec names is a POPULATED but never-read field, and a field that startup refuses to let you populate cannot be populated. The keys remain in the Go type, which is a real residual difference from the spec's own Config declaration and is recorded here as such -- the contract's symbol list does not include Config, so sharing it is a decision beyond what the contract asked for, not a discharge of it.

Reason for not taking the recommendation: a separate Config plus validate would duplicate the coefficient table, the transfer model, the engine agreement, the signal bindings, the shadow-table settings, and the estimator selection across the two arms -- every one of which MUST be identical between them, and every one a place where a copy can drift. It would also destroy the strongest test of that identity: TestOverlayIsCommonModeWithTheFocalArmOutsideTheObjective compares the two shipped overlays field by field, which is only possible because they decode to one type. With two types that test becomes a hand-maintained field mapping, which is the drift the contract exists to prevent. So the trade taken is: one Config type, arm-gated validation, the absence enforced and tested from both directions (TestConfigRejectsTheSLOValueHalf and TestOverlayCarriesNoSLOValueConfig for 'nothing may set it', TestNoSLOValueConfigReachesThisObjective for 'nothing reads it').

The expert also confirmed independently that --allow-experimental-plugins is expressible, that no line-length or complexity linter is enabled at this pin, and that `go test` on the leastttftjoint path failed before this arm existed only because the directory was absent -- a directory with no test files exits 0 -- so that gate line had no independent failure mode.

ROUND 1 REVIEW: three issues raised, all fixed.

(1) The per-algorithm generated tree was absent -- generated/leastttftjoint/ held only the overlay and the manifest. Materialised from the CHECKOUT rather than from snapshot v3, because v3's runner.go predates the shared-Beta-paragraph correction. Verified afterwards that every declared path is byte-identical to the checkout and that the tree holds nothing undeclared.

(2) The focal arm's manifest and generated tree were stale with respect to the seam: files_created omitted arm.go and evalfixture.go, and eight files in its generated tree were pre-seam. Both fixed, and extended beyond what was asked for the reason recorded above -- adding only those two files would have removed the orphaned-shared-package failure while leaving its mirror, an orphaned comparator package, which I measured as a real gate failure rather than inferring. Both manifests now declare the same 35-path union and both trees carry byte-identical copies. The focal arm's description field was NOT touched: the team lead owns it and was editing it concurrently, so only files_created was rewritten, read-modify-write.

(3) objective.go's claim that the producers are 'declared once in the BASELINE overlay and inherited' was false. custom-plugins.yaml is a scalar string, so a treatment overlay REPLACES the baseline's inner config outright and both treatment overlays re-declare token-producer and approx-prefix-cache-producer themselves. Nothing is inherited; the shared binding is an agreement restated by hand across three files. The comment now says that, and says the consequence that matters -- editing the producers in the baseline changes NEITHER arm, so both treatment overlays must be edited and must still agree afterwards. The matching test gap is closed: TestOverlayIsCommonModeWithTheFocalArmOutsideTheObjective compared only the producer NAMES each arm binds, so two overlays could bind the same tokenizedPromptProducerName while declaring token-producer with a different vllm.url. It now compares the full producer ENTRIES (name and decoded parameters) across the two shipped overlays. Verified non-vacuous by perturbing this arm's vllm.url to localhost:9999 and confirming the test fails with 'the two shipped overlays declare token-producer differently', then restoring.

Also taken up, though not requested: EvalFixture's doc comment now records that it never calls startSweeper, so a fixture-built shadow table never reaps and TTL behaviour is not covered there.

ROUND 1 REVISED REVIEW (crossed with the round-2 submission): its item 1 and item 3 were already fixed in round 2. Its NEW item 2b -- that refreshing the focal generated tree put the both-arms runner.go into it while the focal manifest declared no leastttftjoint path, so the focal declared tree would not compile -- was found and fixed independently in round 2 by the same union change, and the reviewer's preferred remedy (option (a): add this arm's 6 paths to the focal manifest and make both 35 and symmetric) is exactly what was done. Verified: each arm's declared tree now carries 29 files of the shared package and 6 of the comparator package, so either arm's runner.go has both packages laid down beside it.

ONE FURTHER CLAUSE ADDED AT THE REVIEWER'S REQUEST. The specification names TWO prohibitions for this arm -- "NO tau FIELD, AND NO NomPrefillTokens" (algorithms/least_ttft_joint.go:237-242) -- and only the tau one is findable in rejectSLOValueConfig's five-key list. NomPrefillTokens is Capacity.NomPrefillTokens, refused by the `capacity` entry rather than by name, because the check is Capacity != (Capacity{}) and rejects the whole block. A reader checking the spec's two prohibitions against the five keys would otherwise conclude the second had been missed, so rejectSLOValueConfig's doc comment now states where it is enforced and why the spec gives it -- muDNom and muPNom take their arguments by parameter, so the shared Coeffs methods compile with no Config field for them and this arm calls neither.

FOCAL BEHAVIOUR PRESERVATION, measured independently of the reviewer at the team lead's request. The approved snapshot (snapshots/causalsloexternality/v4) and the post-refactor checkout both hold 188 test functions in the focal package with IDENTICAL sorted name lists -- nothing removed, renamed, or weakened -- and `go test -count=1 -v` over the checkout reports 188 PASS with 0 FAIL and 0 SKIP. Every published focal margin was established against the pre-refactor code, so this is the check that matters: the four production-file changes each reduce to a no-op for an objective whose ReadsSLOValueConfig() is true, and the three test-file changes are the mechanical validate/newPolicy signature updates.

WHAT files_created MEANS UNDER THE UNION, stated durably because the field's meaning changed and the change is easy to misread as sloppiness. It means THE TREATMENT SOURCE SET -- the files restore_baseline must remove to reach baseline and restore_treatment must lay down to reach treatment -- and NOT "the files this port authored". It has to, because the two arms share one Go package and one registration file that registers both, so neither arm's subset compiles alone: simulating restore_baseline with per-arm subsets produced `no required module provides package .../causalsloexternality` from the gate's own vet. The authorship reading was never what pipeline/lib/source_toggle.py consumed; it only coincided with the treatment source set while there was one arm.

THE INVARIANT THAT MAKES THE UNION CHECKABLE IN ONE LINE, contributed by the round-2 review and verified here independently: for BOTH manifests the declared set (35 files_created plus cmd/epp/runner/runner.go in files_modified) equals EXACTLY the git-dirty set of the target checkout, 36 paths, set-identical in both directions. So restore_baseline driven from either manifest returns the tree to pristine HEAD with nothing stranded and nothing missed. That holds by construction rather than by one measured instance, which is strictly stronger than the toggle simulation that found the problem.
